page.title: Journal
page.purpose: Answer 'who did this, as whom, on whose authority, and when' for any action this scenario has ever taken — including the ones it refused.

priorities.statement: Refusals are as prominent as successes. A refused act-as or a refused release is what an audit actually comes here to find.
Every row carries the full chain — authorising human, persona, run — because a row that names only one of the three cannot answer the question.
The log is visibly append-only; the interface offers no edit or delete affordance anywhere.
Export is a first-class action, not buried.
priorities.notes: An audit trail that cannot leave the machine is not an audit trail.

states.description: A filter is applied; the active filter and the resulting count are both stated.
Entries load but chain resolution for some rows is incomplete; those rows say so rather than showing a blank actor.
Entries are served from cache during an outage. Explicitly labelled, because a partial audit view presented as complete is worse than no view.
